A country of distinct experiences

Different Worlds. One Destination.

From sacred forest to savanna, earthen cities to lagoon nightlife: six places that show how much ground one journey through Nigeria can cover.

Illustration
Osun State·South West·Culture & heritage

Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove

On the edge of Osogbo, a stretch of high forest follows the meandering Osun River. It is one of the last areas of primary high forest in southern Nigeria and a sacred place: the home of Osun, the Yoruba deity associated with water and fertility.

Designation: UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed 2005.

Discover Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove →

Illustration
Cross River State·South South·Nature & adventure

Obudu Mountain Resort

Formerly known as the Obudu Cattle Ranch, the resort sits on the Obudu Plateau in the far north-east of Cross River State. The altitude brings a noticeably cooler climate, rolling grassland and mist that settles in the valleys.

Visiting arrangements: Confirm access, opening times and any fees with the site operator or state tourism office before travelling.

Discover Obudu Mountain Resort →

Illustration
Kano State·North West·Culture & heritage

Kano old city and dye pits

Kano was a major terminus of trans-Saharan trade for centuries. Its old city holds remains of the ancient city walls, the Emir's palace and earthen buildings, some decorated with relief patterns.

Before you go: Read current official travel advice for Kano State before planning a visit.

Discover Kano old city and dye pits →

Illustration
Bauchi State·North East·Nature & adventure

Yankari National Park

Yankari is one of Nigeria's best-known wildlife areas: open savanna and woodland in Bauchi State that supports elephants, antelope, primates and many bird species.

Access: Arrange visits through park authorities and check current official travel advice for Bauchi State.

Discover Yankari National Park →

Illustration
Niger State·North Central·Nature & adventure

Zuma Rock

Zuma Rock rises abruptly from the plain near Madalla in Niger State, just outside the Federal Capital Territory. Most travellers see it from the Abuja–Kaduna road, where its sheer, streaked faces dominate the horizon.

Viewing: Most visitors view the rock from the roadside area. Climbing is not a standard visitor activity.

Discover Zuma Rock →

Illustration
Lagos State·South West·Food & culinary

Lagos food, music and creative scene

Lagos is where much of Nigeria's creative economy is made and performed: music, film, fashion, visual art and design. Galleries, live music venues and restaurants cluster on the Island, Ikoyi, Victoria Island and Lekki, while the mainland has its own markets, street food and nightlife.

Planning: Lagos traffic is heavy. Group activities by area and allow generous travel time between districts.

Discover Lagos food, music and creative scene →

Invest in tourism

Help Build the Next Chapter of Nigerian Tourism.

Destination Nigeria is a proposed national tourism development, investment and destination-marketing platform that brings public institutions, states, businesses, communities and creative partners together to improve the visitor journey and strengthen Nigeria's tourism economy.

Investment-ready products depend on the whole visitor journey working. The platform maps opportunities to each stage, so investors, states and partners can see who needs to act and where.

  1. Discovery
  2. Trip planning
  3. Travel authorization
  4. Arrival
  5. Movement
  6. Accommodation
  7. Attractions
  8. Events
  9. Post-visit feedback

Flagship programme

National Tourism Week

A proposed seven-day national convening that links tourism promotion to practical improvement across the visitor journey, backed by an eight-week campaign and a 12-month action agenda.
